column1: # One row per bundle the image runtime can load. A model_id names the set of
# artifacts that produce one image together, and remote/image-registry.sh
# resolves each component slot against remote/image-artifacts.tsv by
# component_type, so a bundle states its composition rather than a loader
# inferring it from filenames.
# The four component slots read one of three things. An artifact_id names a
# separate file the runtime loads beside the trunk. `packaged` states that the
# diffusion artifact carries that component inside itself, which is what a
# single-file Stable Diffusion checkpoint does with its CLIP text encoder and
# its VAE decoder. `-` states that the bundle omits the component, which is
# what every row without a LoRA reads. The three tokens separate cases a single
# `-` merges: sd15-base decodes with the VAE inside v1-5-pruned-emaonly, and
# sd15-lcm-v1 decodes with sd-vae-ft-mse as a distinct file, and a placement
# arm that moves the decoder to the CPU needs to know which.
# diffusion_artifact always resolves to a `diffusion` artifact, because the
# denoising trunk is the one component no checkpoint packages inside another.
# vae_artifact resolves to either a `vae` or a `tae` component_type. sdxs-512
# names sdxs-512-vae, whose artifact row now reads `tae`: the file is a Tiny
# AutoEncoder rather than a full VAE, and stable-diffusion.cpp's own metadata
# check refuses it under the full-VAE loading path
# (evidence/image-appliance/sdxs-512-standalone/README.md, probe-forms). A
# `tae` artifact reaches sd-cli through the runtime's own --taesd flag rather
# than through the directory's vae/ slot the packaged and `vae` cases use, so
# a launcher resolving this slot to a bundle argv branches on the artifact's
# component_type to choose which flag carries the file.
# native_width and native_height are the resolution the publisher trained the
# trunk at, and default_steps, default_sampler, and default_cfg are the
# publisher's own sampling recipe. They describe the model rather than admit a
# request: a profile in remote/image-profiles.tsv chooses the served width,
# height, steps, sampler, and cfg, and its own max_dimension and max_steps
# bound them.
# default_sampler comes from the stable-diffusion.cpp scheduler vocabulary,
# because that runtime is the one the first campaign pins and a sampler name it
# rejects would fail at the argv rather than in this file.
# tier carries the same closed vocabulary remote/models.tsv uses. Every row
# reads `candidate`: the architecture, the resolution, and the recipe are read
# from the publisher, and no image has been generated on the appliance, so
# quality and throughput stay unqualified while no device failure exists. A row
# reaches `production` when a profile of it has generated an approved image
# with retained telemetry, and `quarantine` when remote/image-quarantine.tsv
# carries a reason record for it.
